notes:
Summary: Ridgeview Assistix is an e-commerce CX platform with ~120 support agents. Evaluating Redwood to replace a brittle rule-based agent-assist + webhook layer that currently calls Zendesk and Stripe APIs. Primary interest: reliable tool-calling (create/update ticket, issue refunds, escalate to L2) + contextual agent assist and ticket summarization.

Key requirements / constraints:
- Tool-calls must be idempotent and auditable; must produce an immutable audit entry in the ticket (Zendesk) and send back correlation id.
- Refund flows: call payments API (Stripe) via a vaulted token; Redwood integration must support tokenized tool-calls or proxy through customer VPC.
- Spike resilience: Black Friday style bursts — expect ~500 concurrent agent requests at peak, ~2000 calls/minute during flash events. Must not drop agent assist suggestions or tool-calls.
- Latency targets: suggestions to agent UI < 250ms median, ticket create/update < 500ms acceptable for sync flows; async webhook fallback acceptable for heavy spikes.
- Model/fallback policy: prefer higher-quality LLM for agent-assist (gpt-like open-model) with automatic fallback to smaller quantized model under sustained load. Need routing by cost/latency.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO (SAML) for admin console, audit logging (per-tool-call), KMS integration for keys, data residency: primary US, EU subset for EU customers.
- Observability: per-request trace id that maps back to Zendesk ticket, Redwood trace, and internal Kibana logs.
- SDKs & onboarding: prefer Python + TypeScript SDK examples; want a reference pattern for safe tool-calls (confirm-buttons, dry-run mode).
